hints: Focus on where the double bonds are in each molecule, as complete saturation will remove all differences due to C=C position.
Recall that hot concentrated acidified KMnO4 cleaves each C=C completely, with =CH2 giving CO2, =CH- giving an acid, and tri- or tetra-substituted C giving a ketone.
For bromine addition, draw the tetrabromo products and check each carbon for four different groups to count chiral centres and compare Br positions.
walkthrough:
**Compare the skeletons**

Both compounds are C10H16 isomers with a 1-methylcyclohex-1-ene ring. The difference is only in the side-chain double bond.

Limonene has $\text{ring-C(CH}_3\text{)=CH}_2$ (terminal alkene) while terpinolene has $\text{ring=C(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ (tetrasubstituted exocyclic alkene).

**Check statement 1, excess H2 / Ni**

Excess hydrogen adds across every C=C:
$$\text{C=C + H}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{Ni}} \text{CH-CH}$$
Both double bonds in both molecules become single. Both give 1-methyl-4-(propan-2-yl)cyclohexane, often called p-menthane. So statement 1 is correct.

**Check statement 2, hot concentrated KMnO4 cleavage**

Vigorous oxidation cleaves C=C. The ring C1=C2 bond is the same in both, giving one end as $\text{CH}_3\text{-C(=O)-}$ (ketone) and the other as $\text{-COOH}$ (from aldehyde oxidation).

The side-chain cleavage is different: limonene $\text{-C(CH}_3\text{)=CH}_2$ gives $\text{-COCH}_3$ + $\text{CO}_2$, terpinolene $\text{-C=C(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ gives ring $\text{>C=O}$ + $\text{(CH}_3\text{)}_2\text{C=O}$. Combined with the opened ring, each gives a molecule with two ketones and one acid, but with the ketone in a different position. So different diketo acids, statement 2 is correct.

**Check statement 3, excess Br2**

Excess $\text{Br}_2$ adds twice:
$$\text{C=C + Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{CBr-CBr}$$
Both give $\text{C}_{10}\text{H}_{16}\text{Br}_4$ with Br atoms in different places, so they are positional isomers. This part is true.

Count chiral carbons at A Level: limonene product has three chiral centres, the two ring C-Br carbons plus the side-chain $\text{C(Br)(CH}_3\text{)(CH}_2\text{Br)}$. Terpinolene product has only two chiral centres, the two ring C-Br carbons, because the side-chain $\text{C(Br)(CH}_3\text{)}_2$ has two identical methyl groups and the ring C-Br is joined to two $\text{CH}_2$ ring groups. So the number of chiral carbons is not the same. Statement 3 is incorrect.

**Conclude**

Statements 1 and 2 only are correct, which corresponds to option B.

options.A: Claims 1, 2 and 3 are all correct. Statements 1 and 2 are correct but 3 is false because the tetrabromo products do not have the same number of chiral carbons (3 for limonene versus 2 for terpinolene at A Level).
options.B: Claims 1 and 2 only are correct. This is right: full hydrogenation gives the same alkane, and vigorous KMnO4 cleavage gives different diketo acids, while statement 3 fails on the chiral count.
options.C: Claims 2 and 3 only are correct. Statement 2 is correct but statement 3 is false and statement 1 is true, so this combination is wrong.
options.D: Claims 1 only is correct. Statement 1 is correct but statement 2 is also correct, so 1 alone is incomplete.
